guideTitle: 7 Best Dustpan and Brush Sets in 2026
metaTitle: Best Dustpan and Brush Sets in 2026
metaDescription: Seven handheld dustpan and brush sets compared on lip seal, bristle shape, built-in combs, snap-together storage and grip, from OXO to Casabella.
introParagraphs: A dustpan and brush set is one of those tools you only notice when it fails. A stiff plastic lip leaves a line of dust behind, a brush that flops over pushes crumbs around, and a set that will not store neatly ends up on the floor of the pantry. The better sets solve these small annoyances with a soft lip, a well shaped brush and a storage clip.

Handheld sets are meant for stoops, stairs, corners, countertops and quick cleanups where a full broom is overkill. They also help anyone who finds a long handle awkward, because a short brush gives close control. The details that matter are how flush the pan lies on the floor, how the bristles reach into corners and whether the pieces snap together.

We evaluated seven distinct handheld sets based on product specs and buyer feedback on each listing. We left out long-handled broom combos, which belong in a separate comparison, and skipped duplicate listings from the same brand. Where a spec is not on the listing, we say to check the product page.

products.name: OXO Good Grips Dustpan & Brush Set
products.description:
The OXO set is the most balanced everyday handheld here. The whisk-broom brush shape lets you sweep from above and reach into corners, and the nylon bristles are listed as part of the design. The dustpan has a soft, flexible lip that covers its entire width and conforms to surfaces, which is the feature that decides whether fine dust gets picked up.

The brush snaps into the dustpan for storage, so the two pieces stay together in a drawer or cabinet. The listing describes the set as portable, and the shape suits quick jobs on counters and floors. The tradeoff is that it does not mention a built-in comb for cleaning the bristles, unlike the Casabella or WDDBHSKN, so you will shake or tap the brush clean.

In use, it is the set you can hand to anyone without explanation. Compared with the Fabuloso, which is the cheapest in this group by position, the OXO gives a softer lip and more refined shape. Compared with the Casabella, it has a simpler brush without the pointed tip, so it suits flat surfaces more than tight cracks.
products.bestFor: Everyday cleanup that needs a dependable soft lip and a simple design.

cons: No built-in comb is mentioned for cleaning bristles
Less specialized for cracks than a pointed brush

products.name: Casabella Wayclean Handheld Angled Dustpan and Brush Set
products.description:
The Casabella Wayclean is built for the awkward places. The angled brush has a pointed tip with rubber bumpers, which the listing says reach corners and cracks while protecting walls. The dustpan has a soft rubber lip that lies flat against the floor to improve pickup.

A built-in comb on the dustpan lets you clean dust and hair off the brush without touching it, which is a real convenience for pet owners and anyone who sweeps hair. The listing calls the size medium, so check the product page for exact dimensions. The tradeoff is that its pointed brush is less of a general whisk, so wide flat sweeping may take a few more strokes.

It suits stair edges, baseboards and tight corners. Against the OXO, you gain the comb and bumper protection, while losing the broad whisk shape. Compared with the NACENA mini at a smaller size, the Casabella is a better fit for a full sized floor corner.

products.name: WDDBHSKN Dustpan and Brush Set with Comb
products.description:
The WDDBHSKN set uses PET fiber bristles and an ergonomic non-slip grip on the hand broom. The listing highlights a wide lip on the dustpan, meant to maximize surface contact, and built-in scraper and comb teeth that pull pet and human hair out of the bristles with one swipe.

The comb teeth are the reason to choose it. Hair tangles in bristles faster than dust does, and a pan that cleans the brush saves a messy step. The tradeoff is that this is a less established name than OXO or Casabella, so check the product page for dimensions, lip material and how the pieces store.

It is a practical pick for homes with shedding pets or long hair. Against the OXO, the comb adds convenience while the OXO leads on lip softness. Against the NACENA, which has silicone edges, the WDDBHSKN focuses on hair removal rather than the seal.

products.name: NACENA Mini Broom and Dustpan Set
products.description:
The NACENA set uses high-density ultra-fine fiber bristles, which the listing says pick up small debris, dust and crumbs. The dustpan edges are sealed with flexible silicone strips that fit tightly against a tabletop and prevent spillage when dumping, and the handle is described as anti-slip.

The silicone edge is the standout. It conforms to uneven surfaces and keeps fine dust from escaping under the lip. The handle is electroplated ABS, which looks tidy but may feel less soft than a rubber grip. Because this is a mini set, it suits tabletops and small spills more than large floor jobs.

It fits counters, desks and quick crumb cleanups. Compared with the OXO, it is smaller and more specialized for crumbs. Compared with the Amazon Basics 2-pack, you get a single set with silicone edges rather than two basic ones.
products.bestFor: Countertop and tabletop crumbs where a tight seal matters.

products.name: MR.SIGA Dustpan and Brush Set with Bamboo Handle
products.description:
The MR.SIGA set has a natural bamboo handle, which gives it a more decorative look than plastic sets. The listing describes dense, durable bristles that will not scratch surfaces, and a soft rubber lip that lies flat on the floor. The handle snaps into the dustpan, and a hanging loop allows wall storage.

It is described for kitchens, offices, bathrooms and garages. The bamboo handle is a design feature, so check the product page for care guidance, because natural wood and moisture do not always mix. The tradeoff is that it lacks the built-in comb found on the Casabella and WDDBHSKN.

It suits a kitchen where the tool hangs in view. Against the OXO, you trade a standard grip for a bamboo one. Against the Fabuloso, the MR.SIGA adds a soft rubber lip and more refined look.

products.name: Fabuloso Brush and Dustpan Set
products.description:
The Fabuloso set is a compact hand broom and dustpan sized for quick everyday cleanups. The listing says the brush and pan clip together into one piece for storage in a cabinet, drawer or caddy, and a hanging hole allows wall mounting.

The sloped pan design is meant to guide debris into the pan with fewer passes. The listing does not describe the lip material or bristle type, so check the product page before assuming a soft rubber lip. It is the cheapest in this group by listing position, which makes it a sensible spare for a garage or second bathroom.

Against the OXO, you give up the soft lip and polish for a lower price. Against the MR.SIGA, it is plainer but easier to replace. It is the simplest set here to hand to a teenager or a guest.

products.name: Amazon Basics Small Portable Mini Dustpan and Brush Set, Pack of 2
products.description:
The Amazon Basics pack includes two mini dustpan and brush sets. The listing says they are made from polypropylene and PET plastic with a flush rubber lip on the dustpan edge and an angled brush with flexible bristles that collects fine dust from corners.

Two sets change how you use them. One can live in the kitchen and the other in a bathroom or car. The tradeoff is size, because mini sets handle crumbs and small piles but are slower on larger spills. The listing is about hand sweeping surfaces, so do not expect broom performance.

Against the NACENA mini, you get two sets rather than one with silicone edges. Against the OXO, they are smaller and less refined, but you get a spare.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The lip decides whether the pan actually picks up fine dust. A soft, flexible lip that spans the full width, like the OXO Good Grips or Casabella Wayclean, closes the gap where dust escapes, while a rigid lip leaves a visible line. The NACENA goes further with silicone strips along the pan edge. Run a finger along the lip and bend it; if it does not give, expect leftover dust.

Bristles should be dense enough to catch fine dust but flexible enough to flick debris into the pan. The OXO uses a whisk-broom shape with nylon bristles, the NACENA uses high-density ultra-fine fiber, and the WDDBHSKN lists PET fibers. Splayed bristles leave crumbs behind after months of use. Look for a compact head that holds its shape.

Hair tangles in bristles faster than dust does, so a comb on the pan rim saves cleaning time. The Casabella has a built-in comb and the WDDBHSKN lists scraper and comb teeth. The OXO, MR.SIGA and Fabuloso do not mention one. If you have pets or long hair, treat this as a requirement.

Corners and cracks need a tip that gets in without scratching. The Casabella has a pointed tip with rubber bumpers that protect walls, while the OXO whisk shape is better on flat surfaces. Mini sets like the NACENA fit tight gaps but cover less area. Decide whether you sweep corners, counters or open floor most.

A set that stays in one piece is far less likely to get lost. The OXO, MR.SIGA and Fabuloso listings say the brush snaps into the pan, and the MR.SIGA and Fabuloso add hanging holes. Check that the brush bristles are covered when stored, because bent bristles ruin the sweep. A hanging loop is helpful in small kitchens.

Handheld sets range from mini to medium, and size affects both control and capacity. The Amazon Basics pack and NACENA are mini, while the Casabella is listed as medium. A non-slip grip, like the one on the WDDBHSKN, helps with wet hands. Choose a size that suits your typical mess, not your biggest one.

howWeEvaluated.title: Dust pickup design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared lip and pan design, since that is where most sets fail. The OXO and Casabella list soft rubber lips, the NACENA uses silicone edges and the Amazon Basics lists a flush rubber lip. We based this on product specs and buyer feedback, not measurements.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brush performance
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at bristle material, shape and tip. The OXO whisk shape suits flat surfaces, the Casabella pointed tip suits corners, and the NACENA fine fibers suit crumbs. We noted where a listing did not specify bristle type.

howWeEvaluated.title: Hair and cleaning features
howWeEvaluated.description: Built-in combs reduce the effort of cleaning bristles. The Casabella and WDDBHSKN lead here, while the OXO, MR.SIGA and Fabuloso do not mention combs. We weighed this heavily for pet households.

howWeEvaluated.title: Storage and portability
howWeEvaluated.description: Snap-together designs and hanging loops matter in small homes. The OXO, MR.SIGA and Fabuloso snap together, and the MR.SIGA and Fabuloso add hanging features. The Amazon Basics 2-pack stores easily in separate rooms.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and lineup role
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed each set by its job. OXO is the overall pick, Casabella leads corners, WDDBHSKN leads pet hair, NACENA leads seal, MR.SIGA leads looks, Fabuloso leads budget storage and Amazon Basics leads multi-room use.

faq.q: What makes a good dustpan and brush set?
faq.a: A soft, flexible lip that sits flat on the floor is the most important feature. Next comes a brush that is dense enough to catch dust and shaped to reach corners. Sets like the OXO and Casabella combine both. A snap-together design or hanging hole helps you keep it handy.

faq.q: Why does my dustpan leave a line of dust?
faq.a: A rigid or warped lip does not seal against the floor. A soft rubber lip, like those on the OXO and Casabella, or a silicone edge like the NACENA, closes that gap. Sweeping toward the pan at a low angle also helps. If the lip is already worn, replace the set.

faq.q: How do I clean hair out of the brush?
faq.a: A comb on the dustpan rim does it in one pull. The Casabella has one built in and the WDDBHSKN lists scraper and comb teeth. Without a comb, tap the brush against a hard edge and pull hair by hand. Do this before storing, so the bristles hold their shape.

Mini sets are good for tabletops, desks and small crumbs. The NACENA and Amazon Basics sets are examples. They are slower on larger spills because the pan holds less. If you sweep stairs or floors, choose a larger set like the OXO or Casabella.

Yes, bristles bend and splay with use, especially when stored pressed against a surface. Sets that snap together with the bristles covered, such as the OXO, protect them better. Replace the set when the brush stops flicking dust into the pan. Check durability feedback on the product page.

It is a design choice rather than a performance upgrade. The MR.SIGA uses natural bamboo for a warmer look. Bamboo can be affected by prolonged moisture, so check the product page for care guidance. If you want maximum durability around water, a plastic handle may be simpler.

faq.q: Can I use a handheld set outdoors?
faq.a: Some listings mention garages and indoor-outdoor use, such as the MR.SIGA and Amazon Basics. Soft bristles work best on dry dust and light debris. They are not ideal for wet leaves or gravel. For large outdoor jobs, a full broom is a better tool.
